documents.name: Universal Modder
documents.description: Install Universal Modder for your coding agent, check game-specific field notes and asset costs, then verify a small local mod in the running game.
documents.introduction:
## What is Universal Modder?

[Universal Modder](https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder) is an open-source toolkit of agent skills, command-line tools and shared field notes for modifying PC games you own. It connects a coding agent's planning and code changes with engine research, asset preparation and checks inside the running game.

Its broad engine coverage is a starting point for investigation, not a compatibility guarantee for every title or version. A community example working on one installation does not establish that the same route works with a different release or mod loader.

This documentation-based tutorial was checked November 5, 2026. No game was modified and no installation or compatibility test was performed for this listing.

## Find the official GitHub project

The upstream repository is `rehan-remade/universal-modder`. Start there for the installation commands, current dependencies and knowledge-base index rather than treating a similarly named download as official.

The checked README documents integrations for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and OpenCode, plus a skills-only option. The installation route affects which components are available.

For **Universal Modder Claude** setup, the README gives these two separate plugin commands:

```text
/plugin marketplace add rehan-remade/universal-modder
/plugin install universal-modder@universal-modder
```

Review the plugin contents and the workspace it will operate in before starting a task. This installs tooling; it does not establish that a particular game has been detected or modified.

## Check the CLI separately

The project includes a Python command named `um`. Its README notes that some agent installation paths expose it automatically, while others require a separate installation:

```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder
```

Git, Python 3.10 or later and ffmpeg are listed requirements. Blender is needed for the documented 3D-to-sprite rendering path. Use each command's `--help` output to check its current options.

Installing only skills is different from having the CLI, asset-generation integration and a working game environment. Confirm the components your first task needs instead of installing every optional service.

## Start with research and one small change

The documented workflow begins by searching prior field notes and identifying the game's engine, version and modding route.

A first read-only knowledge lookup can be:

```bash
um kb search "your game name"
```

Read the matching note's exact version, route, status and verification evidence. The index contains both working and in-progress notes; appearing in the index does not mean a mod is complete.

Before asking an agent to edit files, record the installed game version, existing loader and relevant save locations. Keep a recoverable copy of the saves and mod configuration.

Choose a small, observable first change in a game and mode where you are permitted to mod. For example, change one local asset or one supported gameplay value, then verify that the game starts and the intended behavior appears.

## What the workflow actually covers

The toolkit separates reconnaissance, code or format research, implementation, asset production, in-game automation, recording and packaging.

Its agent skills provide engine-specific playbooks. Those instructions guide investigation; the agent still needs to inspect the actual version it is working with and demonstrate a valid route.

The README's contribution rules exclude cheating other players, distributing game files and publishing decompiled dumps. Keep distributable outputs limited to material you are allowed to share, with the appropriate credits.

For a tutorial, the useful question is whether a specific mod can be built, loaded, exercised and removed. A generated project or a successful compilation alone answers only part of that question.

## Budget model and asset costs separately

The repository is MIT licensed. That does not include a coding-agent subscription, model API usage or generated assets.

The project documents fal for image, 3D, audio and other generation tasks. It also links separate paid sprite services and a local ComfyUI route. Each has its own setup and cost model.

A local asset workflow may avoid a hosted generation charge while using your own hardware resources. A hosted request can cost money even if the generated asset is unsuitable for the game.

Keep credentials in the supported protected runtime or credential store. Do not paste them into prompts, field notes or a public mod package. Review a small asset batch at the game's actual camera scale before generating a full collection.

## Verify in the running game

For the first mod, use an explicit acceptance sequence:

1. Confirm the intended game version and loader.
2. Build and inspect the exact output files.
3. Load the mod in the intended local environment.
4. Exercise the changed behavior and inspect logs.
5. Check that unrelated baseline behavior still works.
6. Disable the mod and confirm the expected recovery path.

Record failures and incomplete checks. Screenshots are useful evidence for visible behavior, while logs and reproducible steps help diagnose loading or runtime problems.

The knowledge base can preserve what worked for a later session. A useful note includes versions, symptoms, the chosen route and observed results. It should not relabel an untested theory as a working implementation.

## Related tools and official sources

For skills aimed at building a game project, see [Awesome Gamedev Agent Skills](https://findryai.com/item/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills). For studying a software project before creating a new implementation, see [Craft Anything](https://findryai.com/item/craft-anything).

- [Official Universal Modder README: installation, dependencies, components and costs](https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder)
- [Knowledge-base index: versioned field notes and completion status](https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder/blob/main/knowledge/INDEX.md)

Sources checked November 5, 2026. This guide makes no claim that a listed game, paid generation service or agent integration was tested by Findry AI.
